correctness.rationale: T(n) counts odd t<=n with gcd(t,n)=gcd((t-1)/2,n)=1, T(1)=0. The proof analyzes odd and n=2m (m odd) by residue inclusion-exclusion, and n divisible by 4 by exact periodicity, establishing |2T(n)-n b(n)|<=3^{omega(n)} for b(2^a)=1/2 and b(p^a)=1-2/p at odd p. Chinese remainder divisibility gives independent Bernoulli I_p for any finite prime collection, uniform tail <=sum_{p>y}1/p², and mean approximation O(log³x/x); therefore T(N_x)/N_x converges weakly to X=1/2 prod_p b_p^{I_p} with bounded moments. For positivity, E sum_p I_p(-log b_p)<infty. Finite prime products are injective in inclusion bits: take largest differing q and use q-adic valuation (earlier factor numerator/denominator smaller than q); max finite atom <=prod_{p<=y}(1-1/p)->0, yielding atomlessness of full product. The Dirichlet convolution h=b*mu, h(2)=-1/2,h(odd p)=-2/p, yields C=(3/16)prod_{p odd}(1-2/p²) in sum T(n)=Cx²+O(x log²x). Independent exact coprimality checks n=1..800 confirmed parity and comparison bounds; they do not prove the infinite limiting law.
